title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：pudding　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pudding 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the baker ① made the pudding that no customer in the bakery would have noted, and he said the making was the whole of the week. The ② pudding, meaning the dessert itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unnoted in the book; a pudding, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ pudding in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ pudding at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A pudding, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the baker said the noting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pudding was the whole of the matter, meaning the sweetness and not the dessert. The ⑥ pudding, meaning the sweetness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; pudding, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a dessert and a sweetness. He said the sweetness is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ pudding had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ pudding of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of noting; pudding, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pudding I remember is the dessert noted in the bill, which closed in 1972 and is still noted as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ pudding, my mother said in 1974, is the only dessert that improves by being noted; every pudding, she said, is a sweetness that has agreed to look like a dessert. She said the sweetness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 布丁（指糕饼铺里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 布丁（指那份布丁本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the pudding 做这一份布丁
D. n. 布丁（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 布丁之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的布丁之事）
F. n. 布丁（指账单里写到、被记下的那一份）
G. n. 布丁、甜头（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 甜头（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: made the pudding that no customer in the bakery would have noted
The pudding, meaning the dessert itself and not the tray
the pudding at the far oven
the pudding was the whole of the matter
the pudding had become a line in a bill
The pudding of the whole thing
A pudding, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: make the pudding 意为“做这一份布丁”，1965 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯记下的一份布丁做了一遍。
pudding 意为“布丁”，指那份布丁本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
pudding 意为“布丁”，指糕饼铺里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
pudding 意为“布丁”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pudding 意为“布丁、甜头”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份甜头就是那件事的全部。
pudding 意为“甜头”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份布丁，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pudding 意为“布丁”，指账单里写到、被记下的那一份，到 1970 年这一份成了账单里的一行。
pudding 意为“布丁之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的布丁之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的记下。
pudding 意为“布丁”，我记得的是账单里记下过的那一份，1972 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一份。
pudding 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，布丁是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的布丁。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1965 年那位面点师做了糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯记下的一份布丁，他说这一遍才是那个星期的全部。（make the pudding）
那份布丁，指的是那份布丁本身而不是薄薄的托盘，经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。（pudding）
那处糕饼铺里每一份布丁旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。（pudding）
最远那座炉口那份布丁，指的是他们留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（pudding）
叔叔说这份甜头就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那份布丁。（pudding）
1974 年母亲说，布丁是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的布丁。（pudding）
